title: What is borderline personality disorder? With Carla Sharp, PhD

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about the most frequently diagnosed personality disorder that many of you may never have heard of.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讨论一种最常被诊断出来，但你们许多人可能从未听说过的人格障碍。

sentences.en: But if you have, you might not really understand what it is because even its name is somewhat enigmatic.
sentences.zh: 但如果你听说过，你可能并不真正了解它是什么，因为即使是它的名字也有些令人费解。

sentences.en: Borderline personality disorder is a condition marked by intense emotions that are typically hostile, angry, or depressive in nature.
sentences.zh: 边缘型人格障碍是一种以强烈情绪为特征的疾病，这些情绪通常具有敌意、愤怒或抑郁的性质。

sentences.en: People with BPD may have a history of impulsive behavior and chaotic relationships.
sentences.zh: 边缘型人格障碍患者可能有冲动行为和混乱人际关系的历史。

sentences.en: Many fear being abandoned and may tend to see the world as purely black or white.
sentences.zh: 许多人害怕被抛弃，往往倾向于以非黑即白的方式看待世界。

sentences.en: Some engage in self-harm or suicidal ideation.
sentences.zh: 有些人会有自残或自杀意念。

sentences.en: And what may be the most challenging about this disorder is that many people with BPD are able to project an appearance of total normalcy.
sentences.zh: 而这种障碍最棘手的地方在于，许多边缘型人格障碍患者能够表现出完全正常的样子。

sentences.en: So what makes borderline personality disorder its own diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么让边缘型人格障碍成为一个独立的诊断呢？

sentences.en: How does it affect people's trajectory in life?
sentences.zh: 它如何影响人们的人生轨迹？

sentences.en: How is it different from other personality disorders?
sentences.zh: 它与其他人格障碍有何不同？

sentences.en: How might you tell if someone you know has it or if you yourself might have it?
sentences.zh: 你如何判断你认识的人是否患有此症，或者你自己是否可能患有此症？

sentences.en: And if people with BPD are high-functioning and appear quote-unquote normal, how can the disorder be diagnosed and treated?
sentences.zh: 如果边缘型人格障碍患者功能良好，看起来“正常”，那么这种障碍该如何诊断和治疗呢？

sentences.en: Is it really a discrete mental illness?
sentences.zh: 它真的是一种独立的精神疾病吗？

sentences.en: And what makes BPD controversial among mental health researchers and practitioners?
sentences.zh: 为什么边缘型人格障碍在心理健康研究人员和从业者中存在争议？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Carla Sharp, professor and associate dean for faculty and research at the University of Houston.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是休斯顿大学教授兼教职与研究副院长卡拉·夏普博士。

sentences.en: She is also director of the university's Adolescent Diagnosis Assessment Prevention and Treatment Center and the Developmental Psychopathology Lab.
sentences.zh: 她还是该大学青少年诊断评估预防与治疗中心以及发展精神病理学实验室的主任。

sentences.en: She holds adjunct positions at the University of Texas,
sentences.zh: 她在德克萨斯大学、

sentences.en: Baylor College of Medicine,
sentences.zh: 贝勒医学院、

sentences.en: University College London, and the University of the Free State in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 伦敦大学学院以及南非自由州大学担任兼职职务。

sentences.en: Dr. Sharp has a longstanding interest in social cognition as a cause and correlate of psychiatric disorders across the lifespan, with a special focus on youth.
sentences.zh: 夏普博士长期以来对社会认知作为贯穿生命周期的精神疾病的成因和相关因素感兴趣，特别关注青少年群体。

sentences.en: She has published over 300 peer-reviewed articles, numerous chapters, and eight books.
sentences.zh: 她发表了300多篇同行评审文章、众多章节和八本书。

sentences.en: A large proportion of her research uses borderline personality disorder and other personality pathology to study where social cognitive function goes awry.
sentences.zh: 她的大部分研究利用边缘型人格障碍和其他人格病理学来研究社会认知功能在何处出现偏差。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today, Dr. Sharp.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加节目，夏普博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Kim.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，金。

sentences.en: I'm so glad to be here with you talking about this topic that's very close to my heart.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能在这里与你讨论这个我非常关心的话题。

sentences.en: Well, let's start by talking about personality disorders in general.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们先从人格障碍的总体情况谈起。

sentences.en: How does psychology categorize and define personality and personality disorders?
sentences.zh: 心理学是如何分类和定义人格及人格障碍的？

sentences.en: And how is this area of psychology evolving?
sentences.zh: 心理学的这一领域又是如何演变的？

sentences.en: Well, that is a very big question, and I'm going to try and keep it succinct.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的问题，我会尽量简明扼要地回答。

sentences.en: The diagnosis of personality disorder is a disorder or a diagnosis in transition.
sentences.zh: 人格障碍的诊断是一个处于转型期的诊断。

sentences.en: For the last 20 to 30 years, since the publication of the DSM-3, we have been ascribing to a system of diagnosing personality disorder that we call the categorical system.
sentences.zh: 在过去20到30年里，自《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》第三版（DSM-3）发布以来，我们一直采用一种我们称之为“分类系统”的人格障碍诊断体系。

sentences.en: It is based on a medical model in the sense that we see disorder as something that a person has or does not have.
sentences.zh: 它基于一种医学模型，即我们将障碍视为一个人“有”或“没有”的东西。

sentences.en: You can think a little bit about pregnancy as an example.
sentences.zh: 你可以把怀孕作为一个例子来思考。

sentences.en: You know, you can't be halfway pregnant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人不可能处于“半怀孕”状态。

sentences.en: You're either pregnant or you're not pregnant.
sentences.zh: 你要么怀孕了，要么没怀孕。

sentences.en: And in the same way, in the categorical system of diagnosis, we view someone as having a personality disorder or they don't have a personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 同样地，在分类诊断系统中，我们认为一个人要么有人格障碍，要么没有人格障碍。

sentences.en: Now, this has been the way we've diagnosed personality disorder since the DSM-3, which was published in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 这就是自20世纪80年代出版DSM-3以来我们诊断人格障碍的方式。

sentences.en: However, over the last 20 to 30 years, we have discovered that this categorical system has some limitations to fully understanding and treating personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 然而，在过去20到30年里，我们发现这种分类系统在全面理解和治疗人格障碍方面存在一些局限性。

sentences.en: So, one of the important data points in this regard is that when we take all of the personality disorder symptoms,
sentences.zh: 在这方面，一个重要的数据点是，当我们汇总所有人格障碍的症状时，

sentences.en: and I should just explain first that there are in the categorical system, there are 10 personality disorder, 10 categories of personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 我应该先解释一下，在分类系统中，有10种人格障碍，即10种人格障碍类别。

sentences.en: And one of them is, for instance, BPD that you mentioned, borderline personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是你提到的边缘型人格障碍（BPD）。

sentences.en: Another one is narcissistic personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 另一种是自恋型人格障碍。

sentences.en: A third one is antisocial personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 第三种是反社会型人格障碍。

sentences.en: So, there's 10 of these personality disorders in the current system of diagnosing personality disorders.
sentences.zh: 所以，在当前的人格障碍诊断系统中，有这10种人格障碍。

sentences.en: When you take all of the symptoms of those 10 personality disorders and you put them together into a big factor analysis,
sentences.zh: 当你把这10种人格障碍的所有症状放在一起进行大规模的因素分析时，

sentences.en: you would expect you will get 10 factors pushed out by the factor analysis.
sentences.zh: 你本应期望因素分析会得出10个因素。

sentences.en: This is how factor analysis works.
sentences.zh: 这就是因素分析的工作原理。

sentences.en: If we want to understand a particular phenomenon, we put the signs and symptoms of that phenomenon into a factor analysis
sentences.zh: 如果我们想了解某种特定现象，我们会把该现象的体征和症状放入因素分析中，

sentences.en: and we get one dimension out that explains that phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 然后得出一个解释该现象的维度。

sentences.en: In the case of personality disorder, we want to be able to see if they really exist in nature, like the DSM would suggest, we want to be able to see 10 personality disorders
sentences.zh: 在人格障碍的情况下，如果我们想看看它们是否像DSM所暗示的那样真正存在于自然界中，我们希望看到10种人格障碍，

sentences.en: come out of the factor analysis.
sentences.zh: 从因素分析中得出。

sentences.en: So, we want to see the symptoms of BPD hang together to form borderline personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们希望看到边缘型人格障碍的症状聚集在一起，形成边缘型人格障碍。

sentences.en: We want to see the symptoms of narcissistic personality disorder to hang together to form narcissistic personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 我们希望看到自恋型人格障碍的症状聚集在一起，形成自恋型人格障碍。

sentences.en: Same with antisocial, same with avoidance, same with histrionic, all of those 10 personality disorders.
sentences.zh: 反社会型、回避型、表演型等所有这10种人格障碍也是如此。

sentences.en: What happens in actual fact when you put all of those symptoms into a factor analysis?
sentences.zh: 但当你把所有这些症状放入因素分析时，实际情况如何呢？

sentences.en: It's a big mishmash of dimensions and none of these categories come out very clearly.
sentences.zh: 那是一大堆维度的混合体，没有任何类别能清晰地显现出来。

sentences.en: And so, this has been one of the first and most important signs that these categories don't exist in nature as we have always thought they did.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是第一批也是最重要的迹象之一，表明这些类别并不像我们一直认为的那样存在于自然界中。

sentences.en: In fact, when you do meet criteria for something like BPD, you probably also meet criteria for two or three other personality disorders.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当你符合边缘型人格障碍的标准时，你很可能也符合其他两三种人格障碍的标准。

sentences.en: When you do meet criteria for BPD, you probably also meet criteria, this makes the picture even more complex, for depression and anxiety and substance use disorder.
sentences.zh: 当你符合边缘型人格障碍的标准时，你很可能也符合抑郁症、焦虑症和物质使用障碍的标准，这使得情况变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: We are now at a point in our history in the field where we have decided to move away from this categorical system of personality disorder diagnosis
sentences.zh: 我们现在处于该领域历史上的一个节点，我们决定从这种人格障碍诊断的分类系统转向，

sentences.en: to what we call a more dimensional system.
sentences.zh: 转向我们所说的更具维度的系统。

sentences.en: And so, when you open the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual for Mental Disorders, the DSM, the fifth edition was published in 2013.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你打开《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）时，第五版于2013年出版。

sentences.en: When you open the DSM, you will actually find two parallel systems for diagnosing personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 当你打开DSM时，你会发现实际上有两种并行的系统用于诊断人格障碍。

sentences.en: In section two of the DSM, you will find the old 10 categories.
sentences.zh: 在DSM的第二部分，你会发现旧的10个类别。

sentences.en: BPD will be there, narcissism will be there, antisocial and so forth.
sentences.zh: 边缘型人格障碍会在那里，自恋型会在那里，反社会型等等。

sentences.en: They will all be there.
sentences.zh: 它们都会在那里。

sentences.en: But when you page forward, you will find in section three, the alternative model for personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 但当你往后翻，你会发现第三部分中有人格障碍的替代模型。

sentences.en: And this is the dimensional model for personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 这就是人格障碍的维度模型。

sentences.en: And that is where we are moving towards in the future.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们未来发展的方向。

sentences.en: And I could tell you a little bit more about what that means and why that is important that we are moving towards this dimension.
sentences.zh: 我可以多告诉你一些这意味着什么，以及为什么我们向这个维度发展很重要。

sentences.en: But I'll stop there for now and see if you have any follow-up questions about just the categories to start with.
sentences.zh: 但我现在先停在这里，看看你对这些类别是否还有什么后续问题。

sentences.en: Well, it's very complex.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这非常复杂。

sentences.en: And it's got to be a challenge then for clinicians who are trying to come up with a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 对于试图做出诊断的临床医生来说，这一定是个挑战。

sentences.en: I mean, how could you actually say somebody has BPD if it overlaps with so many other things?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果边缘型人格障碍与这么多其他疾病重叠，你怎么能断定某人患有此症呢？

sentences.en: Are there a certain number of traits, it's a kind of formula that says this person has BPD or has a different disorder?
sentences.zh: 是否存在一定数量的特征，或者某种公式来判定此人患有边缘型人格障碍还是其他障碍？

sentences.en: Well, at the moment, at present, when we use section two of the DSM, which is what most clinicians still use,
sentences.zh: 目前，当我们使用大多数临床医生仍在使用的DSM第二部分时，

sentences.en: clinicians find it relatively straightforward to diagnose someone with BPD in the sense that there are nine criteria.
sentences.zh: 临床医生发现诊断边缘型人格障碍相对直接，因为有九项标准。

sentences.en: So, you know, those criteria are affective instability, so mood instability, anger, suicidality, emptiness,
sentences.zh: 这些标准包括情感不稳定性，即情绪不稳定、愤怒、自杀倾向、空虚感、

sentences.en: identity disturbance, abandonment fears,
sentences.zh: 身份认同障碍、被抛弃恐惧、

sentences.en: relationship problems, and impulsivity.
sentences.zh: 人际关系问题和冲动性。

sentences.en: And so when a clinician meets someone and the person tells them that, you know, they don't know what's going on with them, they have a lot of relationship difficulties.
sentences.zh: 所以，当临床医生遇到一个人，而那个人告诉他们，他们不知道自己怎么了，他们有很多关系上的困难。

sentences.en: They've been on an NS, you know, SSRI for a long time, doesn't seem to be helping.
sentences.zh: 他们长期服用选择性5-羟色胺再摄取抑制剂（SSRI），似乎没什么帮助。

sentences.en: They've tried all kinds of therapy, doesn't seem to be helping.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试了各种治疗，似乎也没什么帮助。

sentences.en: They still have lots of relationship difficulties.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然有很多关系上的困难。

sentences.en: They're self-harm, they're suicidal.
sentences.zh: 他们有自残和自杀倾向。

sentences.en: The clinician will start thinking this may be personality disorder because the person is not responding to traditional treatment approaches
sentences.zh: 临床医生会开始认为这可能是人格障碍，因为此人对传统的治疗方法没有反应，

sentences.en: for depression, anxiety, substance abuse.
sentences.zh: 即针对抑郁、焦虑、药物滥用的治疗。

sentences.en: Usually that tells us that there's something extra going on in the personality functioning domain.
sentences.zh: 通常这告诉我们，在人格功能领域还有额外的问题存在。

sentences.en: And so the clinician can then go through those nine criteria and if the person meets five or more of those nine borderline criteria,
sentences.zh: 因此，临床医生可以逐一核对那九项标准，如果此人符合这九项边缘型标准中的五项或更多，

sentences.en: then the person is deemed to be meeting criteria, clinical threshold for borderline personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 那么该人就被认为符合边缘型人格障碍的临床阈值。

sentences.en: And that's all fine.
sentences.zh: 这没问题。

sentences.en: And the clinician will then simply do what they do currently, which is diagnosed BPD, diagnosed depression, anxiety, substance use disorder, which usually hang together.
sentences.zh: 临床医生会简单地做他们目前所做的事情，即诊断边缘型人格障碍、抑郁症、焦虑症、物质使用障碍，这些通常是共存的。

sentences.en: If they explore a different personality disorder, a person may then meet criteria for another personality disorder as well.
sentences.zh: 如果他们探索另一种人格障碍，此人可能还会符合另一种人格障碍的标准。

sentences.en: And all of that information goes into the person's chart and the clinician has the job to treat all of this co-occurring disorders at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所有这些信息都会进入病人的病历，临床医生有责任同时治疗所有这些共存的障碍。

sentences.en: And I think that is okay.
sentences.zh: 我认为这还可以。

sentences.en: That's how we've been functioning for the last 30 years.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们过去30年的运作方式。

sentences.en: And we have moderate success with that.
sentences.zh: 我们对此取得了适度的成功。

sentences.en: Once a person's been diagnosed with BPD, they usually get one of the frontline treatments for BPD, which is either dialectical behavior therapy, which is most common in the US,
sentences.zh: 一旦一个人被诊断出患有边缘型人格障碍，他们通常会接受边缘型人格障碍的一线治疗之一，即辩证行为疗法（在美国最常见），

sentences.en: or they would get mentalization-based therapy, which is more common in Europe.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会接受心智化疗法，这在欧洲更常见。

sentences.en: There are some other treatment approaches too that are evidence-based, like transference-focused therapies, schema-focused therapy.
sentences.zh: 还有其他一些基于证据的治疗方法，如移情聚焦疗法、图式聚焦疗法。

sentences.en: And actually there's good evidence showing that good old CBT can actually be helpful for people with BPD as well.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有充分证据表明，传统的认知行为疗法（CBT）对边缘型人格障碍患者也有帮助。

sentences.en: So there are ways in which we...
sentences.zh: 所以有一些方法我们……

sentences.en: That's right, cognitive behavioral therapy.
sentences.zh: 没错，认知行为疗法。

sentences.en: So there are ways that we...
sentences.zh: 所以有一些方法我们……

sentences.en: That this system has worked well enough, but we think we can do better.
sentences.zh: 这个系统运作得还算可以，但我们认为我们可以做得更好。

sentences.en: We think with a new system of diagnosis, we can actually be more precise in diagnosing people with personality disorder more generally.
sentences.zh: 我们认为通过新的诊断系统，我们可以更精确地诊断人格障碍患者。

sentences.en: But we can also just make it a little less complex than having this co-occurring mismatch of disorders that each require their own manualized treatment.
sentences.zh: 但我们也可以让它不那么复杂，不必面对这种需要各自手册化治疗的共存障碍的错配。

sentences.en: So the field has been looking for common factors, common dimensions that is shared by all of the personality pathology so that we can simplify this very complex process
sentences.zh: 因此，该领域一直在寻找共同因素，即所有人格病理所共有的共同维度，以便我们能简化这个我刚才概述的非常复杂的过程。

sentences.en: that I've so far outlined.
sentences.zh: 我刚才概述的那个过程。

sentences.en: So how debilitating is BPD among the constellation of personality disorders?
sentences.zh: 那么，在众多人格障碍中，边缘型人格障碍有多大的致残性？

sentences.en: I think it is the most diagnosed personality disorder.
sentences.zh: 我认为它是被诊断最多的人格障碍。

sentences.en: And that is partly due to the fact that BPD appears to capture something that is common among all of the personality disorders.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为边缘型人格障碍似乎捕捉到了所有人格障碍所共有的某种东西。

sentences.en: And I do want to talk a little bit about this dimension that I've been mentioning that is shared by all of the personality disorders.
sentences.zh: 我确实想谈谈我提到的这个所有人格障碍所共有的维度。

sentences.en: So what is this dimensional approach that the field is moving towards that helps us better define personality disorder?
sentences.zh: 那么，该领域正在向什么维度方法发展，以帮助我们更好地定义人格障碍呢？

sentences.en: So if you...
sentences.zh: 所以如果你……

sentences.en: I'm going to go back to factor analysis, which I introduced a little bit earlier as a way of legitimizing disorders, right?
sentences.zh: 我要回到因素分析，我之前稍微介绍过它作为一种使障碍合法化的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: If you actually do factor analyze all of the symptoms of personality disorder, what you do get out of that factor analysis in more recent studies is what we call a general factor,
sentences.zh: 如果你真的对人格障碍的所有症状进行因素分析，在最近的研究中，你从因素分析中得到的是我们所说的“一般因素”，

sentences.en: a general factor of personality functioning.
sentences.zh: 即人格功能的一般因素。

sentences.en: Now, if your listeners have been hearing about how IQ works in the past, they will know that when we think about IQ, we think about a person with an IQ of 100 as having average IQ.

sentences.en: And we think about a person as having an IQ of 120 as above average and a person with 140 as superior, right?

sentences.en: And we would also think about someone at 70 as someone who is lower in IQ.

sentences.en: So there's a common dimension, a general factor of intelligence.

sentences.en: Now, within that general factor of intelligence, we can think about people that are very good at math, but not so good at language.

sentences.en: Or people that are very fast at processing speed, but they're not so good at math.

sentences.en: So we can think about specific ways in which people differ on specific aspects of intelligence, even though their average, their general IQ can be at a certain level.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以想到人们在智力的特定方面存在差异，即使他们的平均智商或一般智商处于某个水平。

sentences.en: The field of personality has moved in that same direction where we, rather than thinking about the 10 categories, we are now thinking about a general personality functioning,

sentences.en: a sort of personality quotient, if you will, rather than an intelligence quotient.

sentences.en: Rather than IQ, we can think about personality quotient.
sentences.zh: 与其谈论智商，我们可以考虑人格商。

sentences.en: And what we want to talk about when we think about your personality functioning is how good are you at managing yourself in the context of interpersonal interactions?
sentences.zh: 当我们考虑你的人格功能时，我们想谈论的是你在人际互动背景下管理自己的能力如何？

sentences.en: How good are you at reading other people's interactions, reading their minds, and managing yourself when you are busy interacting with other people?

sentences.en: So the shorthand version of this is adaptive or maladaptive self and interpersonal functioning.
sentences.zh: 所以简而言之，这就是适应性或非适应性的自我和人际功能。

sentences.en: And that appears to be the general factor of personality functioning.
sentences.zh: 这似乎就是人格功能的一般因素。

sentences.en: How good are we at managing the self in the context of our attachment relationships?
